17"""FlagGems ``mH``: the zero-copy conjugate-transpose view of ``self``. 

18 

19``aten::mH(self)`` is a pure metadata/view operator. It swaps the last two 

20dimensions of ``self`` and toggles the *lazy* conjugate bit; nothing is 

21materialized and no element is read, moved or written. The result therefore 

22shares ``self``'s storage at ``self``'s storage offset, re-derives the strides 

23for the exchanged last-two dimensions (so non-contiguous, transposed, 

24column-strided and offset-window inputs are handled for free), and stays a view 

25of ``self``, so a write through the result is visible in ``self``. 

26 

27Contract points that drive the implementation: 

28 

29* **Never materialize.** No ``conj_physical`` / ``resolve_conj`` / ``clone`` / 

30 ``contiguous`` / ``to`` / eager elementwise negation and no kernel launch: 

31 the result is built purely from view/metadata primitives and shares the 

32 input storage; ``is_conj()`` is the lazy conjugate bit, exactly as aten. 

33* **Conjugation is dtype-dependent and a toggle.** The lazy conjugate bit only 

34 exists for complex dtypes; for a real tensor the rank >= 2 result is exactly 

35 the last-two-dim stride swap. For complex inputs the bit is *toggled* 

36 (``x.mH.mH`` recovers the input layout), including when the input already 

37 carries the bit. 

38* **Rank dispatch.** Rank >= 2 performs the swap; rank 1 is rejected with 

39 ``RuntimeError``; rank 0 is the deprecated path that warns (once per 

40 process, as aten does) and degrades to ``conj()``: for real dtypes that is 

41 the identity (aten hands back the very same object, which this copy 

42 reproduces with ``return self``), for complex dtypes a fresh aliasing view 

43 with the bit set. 

44* **Grad flow.** ``conj`` and ``transpose`` are differentiable views, so the 

45 backward of ``mH`` is the same relayout applied to the upstream gradient. 

46 

47gcu400 local deviation -- dispatcher-neutral view construction: 

48 

49The generic composition ``transpose(conj(self))`` routes each primitive 

50through the torch dispatcher. Inside the production ``use_gems()`` window, 

51``aten::transpose.int`` and ``aten::_conj`` (reached via the ``aten::conj`` 

52composite) are registered FlagGems kernels, so the composition degrades: 

53 

54* real dtypes pay a second Python dispatcher hop through FlagGems' 

55 ``transpose`` kernel (~2.9 us/call direct, ~4.1 us dispatched, vs ~1.3 us 

56 outside the window; interleaved harness, GCU400, 2026-11-17); 

57* complex dtypes land on ``_conj_kernel`` -- an ``empty_like`` + Triton 

58 materializing conjugate copy -- which silently *breaks* the view contract 

59 (``is_conj()`` False, storage not shared) and costs ~35 us/call direct / 

60 ~37 us dispatched. 

61 

62With this revision the same harness measures, inside the ``use_gems()`` 

63window (GCU400, interleaved, 6 shapes x {f32, c64}, 2026-11-17): dispatched 

64``aten::mH`` real 4071-4161 -> 2933-3054 ns (-26..-28%), complex 36760-37682 

65-> 3282-3393 ns (-91%, ~11x); direct calls 2963-3069 -> 1595-1677 ns (real) 

66and 34602-35505 -> 1917-1995 ns (complex); the complex production result 

67regains full aten parity (``is_conj()`` True, shared storage) that the 

68materializing path had silently broken. Outside the window the direct body 

69is ~+0.35 us slower than the old native-transpose composition (permute is a 

70slightly heavier single hop than native transpose, 1441 vs 1116 ns), a 

71context that production never enters and that the official kernel-mode 

72benchmark cannot observe anyway (its event-pair floor is ~2.1 us). 

73 

74This copy therefore builds the same observable state without dispatcher 

75round-trips: 

76 

77* the stride swap uses ``Tensor.permute`` with a cached axis-order tuple 

78 (``aten::permute`` is not registered by FlagGems, so it is a single native 

79 C++ hop in every dispatch context) -- ``permute`` was verified to reproduce 

80 ``transpose(-2, -1)`` shape/stride/offset/storage bit-for-bit on 

81 contiguous, transposed, offset-window, expanded and zero-sized inputs; 

82* the lazy conjugate bit is toggled with the raw C binding 

83 ``torch._C._set_conj`` on the freshly created view (no dispatcher at all), 

84 reproducing aten's ``alias_with_conj`` final state; the input tensor's own 

85 bit is never touched; 

86* complex tensors that require grad (with grad mode enabled) keep the aten 

87 composition ``transpose(conj(self))``: the autograd view metadata is 

88 captured at view-creation time, so a post-hoc bit flip would silently drop 

89 the conjugation from the backward -- the dispatcher hops are only paid on 

90 this cold, correctness-first arm; 

91* if ``torch._C._set_conj`` is unavailable the composition falls back to the 

92 generic chain. 

93 

94Host-path notes: the C-level ``Tensor`` descriptors are bound once at import 

95(no per-call bound-method creation), the axis order is cached per rank in a 

96module dict (no per-call tuple construction), and rank-0 tensors never pay 

97the complex checks. No Triton kernel exists for this operator: there is no 

98elementwise domain and no device payload. 

99""" 

100 

101import logging 

102import warnings 

103 

104import torch 

105 

106logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

107 

108__all__ = ["mH"] 

109 

110_MH_1D_MESSAGE = ( 

111 "tensor.mH is only supported on matrices or batches of matrices. " "Got 1-D tensor." 

112) 

113_MH_0D_MESSAGE = "Tensor.mH is deprecated on 0-D tensors. Consider using x.conj()." 

114 

115# aten emits its deprecation notice once per process; mirror that so the 0-D 

116# timing case does not pay the warnings machinery on every iteration. 

117_MH_WARN_STATE = {"warned": False} 

118 

119# Bind the C-level Tensor descriptors once: ``t.conj()`` otherwise pays a 

120# type-dictionary lookup plus a bound-method creation on every call. 

121_DIM = torch.Tensor.dim 

122_IS_COMPLEX = torch.Tensor.is_complex 

123_IS_CONJ = torch.Tensor.is_conj 

124_PERMUTE = torch.Tensor.permute 

125_AS_STRIDED = torch.Tensor.as_strided 

126_STORAGE_OFFSET = torch.Tensor.storage_offset 

127_TRANSPOSE = torch.Tensor.transpose 

128_CONJ = torch.Tensor.conj 

129_GRAD_ENABLED = torch.is_grad_enabled 

130 

131# Raw C-level conjugate-bit setter (no dispatcher participation). Guarded so 

132# the module still imports and degrades to the aten composition if a build 

133# lacks the binding. 

134try: 

135 _SET_CONJ = torch._C._set_conj 

136except AttributeError: # pragma: no cover - defensive 

137 _SET_CONJ = None 

138 

139# rank -> axis order that exchanges the last two dimensions. 

140_SWAP_PERMS = {} 

141 

142 

143def mH(self): 

144 """Return the zero-copy conjugate-transpose view of ``self``.""" 

145 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME MH") 

146 ndim = _DIM(self) 

147 if ndim < 2: 

148 if ndim == 1: 

149 raise RuntimeError(_MH_1D_MESSAGE) 

150 # 0-D: deprecated aten path, warn once and degrade to conj(). 

151 if not _MH_WARN_STATE["warned"]: 

152 _MH_WARN_STATE["warned"] = True 

153 warnings.warn(_MH_0D_MESSAGE, UserWarning, stacklevel=2) 

154 if not _IS_COMPLEX(self): 

155 # aten: conj() of a real tensor is the identity (same object). 

156 return self 

157 if self.requires_grad and _GRAD_ENABLED(): 

158 return _CONJ(self) 

159 if _SET_CONJ is not None: 

160 out = _AS_STRIDED(self, (), (), _STORAGE_OFFSET(self)) 

161 _SET_CONJ(out, not _IS_CONJ(self)) 

162 return out 

163 return _CONJ(self) 

164 if not _IS_COMPLEX(self): 

165 # Real input: mH is exactly the last-two-dim stride swap. 

166 perm = _SWAP_PERMS.get(ndim) 

167 if perm is None: 

168 perm = _SWAP_PERMS[ndim] = tuple(range(ndim - 2)) + (ndim - 1, ndim - 2) 

169 return _PERMUTE(self, perm) 

170 # Complex input: swap the axes and toggle the lazy conjugate bit. 

171 if self.requires_grad and _GRAD_ENABLED(): 

172 # View metadata (and the conjugation inside it) is captured at 

173 # view-creation time by autograd; flip the bit only when untracked. 

174 return _TRANSPOSE(_CONJ(self), -2, -1) 

175 if _SET_CONJ is not None: 

176 perm = _SWAP_PERMS.get(ndim) 

177 if perm is None: 

178 perm = _SWAP_PERMS[ndim] = tuple(range(ndim - 2)) + (ndim - 1, ndim - 2) 

179 out = _PERMUTE(self, perm) 

180 _SET_CONJ(out, not _IS_CONJ(self)) 

181 return out 

182 return _TRANSPOSE(_CONJ(self), -2, -1)
